subtopicTitle: Diffraction — single slit intensity pattern derivation

cards.front: State the far-field single-slit intensity pattern.
What physical quantity does the parameter $$\beta$$ represent in the single-slit derivation?
cards.back: Half the phase difference between secondary wavelets emitted from the two edges of the slit.

cards.front: Write the infinitesimal electric-field contribution $$dE$$ from a strip of width $$dy$$ at position $$y$$ inside the slit.
Set the integration limits for the slit centered at the origin and evaluate the resulting integral for the total amplitude.
cards.back: Limits $$y=-a/2$$ to $$+a/2$$; integral yields $$E=E_0\frac{\sin\beta}{\beta}$$ with $$\beta=\frac{\pi a\sin\theta}{\lambda}$$

cards.front: Why is the observed intensity proportional to $$|E|^2$$ rather than to the amplitude itself?
cards.back: Detectors measure time-averaged power; the time average of the squared real part of the complex field is proportional to the modulus squared.

cards.front: Show that the first minimum occurs when $$\beta=\pi$$ and recover the familiar slit-width condition.
In the limit $$a\ll\lambda$$, what does the single-slit pattern reduce to and why?
cards.back: It becomes essentially uniform (no diffraction minima); the slit behaves as a point source because $$\beta$$ remains small over all observable angles.
